anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently picks a sub-optimal execution plan despite having reasonably accurate statistics, leading to excessive CPU, memory, or I/O work per statement.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Physical or logical free space in data, temp, log, or backup areas is exhausted or critically low, provoking allocation failures, halted growth, or stalled background maintenance.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Network pathways or connection-handling facilities (listeners, sockets, authentication slots) become saturated or unstable, delaying or preventing session establishment and data transfer.

When these three root causes strike concurrently, the database exhibits a multi-layered degradation pattern: poorly chosen plans inflate I/O and temp-space consumption, quickly driving already tight storage to full exhaustion; as space runs out, sorts, hash spills, log growth, and segment extensions fail, causing sessions to hang. Stalled or killed statements hold server processes and TCP sockets open, so connection pools back up, listener queues overflow, and clients experience mounting time-outs and retransmits. Administrators may observe wildly oscillating execution plans, sudden surges in disk-space usage, a spike in temp-space and redo allocation errors, coupled with escalating counts of refused or half-open connections. The overlap of plan instability, space shortages, and network contention obscures clear attribution—symptoms such as long response times or session drops can originate from any layer, making conventional single-axis diagnostics misleading.

Causally, a sub-optimal plan (e.g., full table scan instead of index access) magnifies I/O volume and temp usage, accelerating space depletion in datafiles and temp segments. Once space alarms trigger, background extensions pause or fail, causing active DML and sort operations to stall; these blocked back-end processes keep network sockets occupied, exhausting connection concurrency limits and increasing client wait times. Conversely, network slowdowns elongate statement runtimes, keeping temp segments and uncommitted redo active for longer periods, which further delays space reclamation and pushes the system toward capacity exhaustion. The vicious circle culminates in a systemic slowdown where optimizer mis-plans, storage full conditions, and network congestion perpetuate and amplify each other, jeopardizing both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
